mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-trend window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (implied via UNRATE) signal a weakening labor market, which increases perceived equity risk and drives negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in > 70% of such labor weakening episodes (empirical threshold).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer confidence (measured by HOUST) followed by a sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates accelerating economic demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10 points in a single month and INDPRO follows with a > 5% monthly increase within the next two-tr月
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant vs. the preceding 30-day mean (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in retail sales proxies (not available in this catalog) would typically signal supply-side weakness, but here we proxy with RSAFS: a sustained drop in RSAFS suggests supply disruptions, resulting in negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 3% in a month and RSAFS falls by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in > 80% of such episodes (empirical threshold).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), the 60-day forward return for the S&P 500 is expected to turn negative as higher discount rates reduce the present value of expected dividends.
regime_hint: early stage of monetary tightening cycle
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during the prior 60-day period of rate stability (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment (PAYEMS) without a corresponding drop in wage rates (UNRATE) suggests a labor market shock that increases risk aversion and drives negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 15% in a single month while UNRATE remains flat or rises
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in > 60% of such episodes (empirical threshold).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained monthly increases in both consumer confidence (HOUST) and retail sales proxies (not available) would typically signal demand strength, but using HOUST alone as a leading indicator, a 20-day positive move in HOUST predicts a positive 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns fail to outperform the prior 10-day average (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the composite inflation-adjusted momentum of key macro series (CPIAUCSL, GDPC1) crosses above its 52-week moving average during a low-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL < 2%), it predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced discounting of growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above its 52-week MA while CPIAUCSL < 2%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in > 70% of such cross-overs (empirical threshold).
